input.quote: 5.3 Sublicenses. AbbVie shall have the right to grant sublicenses (or further rights of reference), through multiple tiers of Sublicensees, under the licenses and rights of reference granted in Sections 5.1.1, 5.1.2 and 5.1.3, to its Affiliates and other Persons; provided that any such sublicenses shall be consistent with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and AbbVie shall remain liable for its obligations under this Agreement and for the performance of all Sublicensees.
input.rationale: The grant to us (AbbVie as licensee under Sections 5.1.1-5.1.3) meets, and in fact exceeds, the fallback position, so we do not redline it. (i) Affiliates: Section 5.3 lets us sublicense through multiple tiers to "its Affiliates and other Persons" with no Harpoon consent (only a post-execution copy), which also captures contractors/third parties acting for us; Sections 5.4, 5.5 and 13.16 reinforce Affiliate rights. This is better than the fallback's "covered on written notice". (ii) Successor transfer: Section 13.4.1 permits assignment "without the other Party's consent to its Affiliate or to a successor, whether in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or any other transaction, of the business to which this Agreement relates", satisfying both the fallback M&A transfer and the preferred successor transfer. (iii) Not revocable at will: Harpoon may terminate only for uncured material breach under Section 12.2.1 (90-day cure), the related diligence provision 12.2.2, or insolvency under Section 12.4 — there is no discretionary revocation. (iv) Paid-up position: Section 12.1.2 provides that on expiry of the Term the Section 5.1.3 grants "shall become non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable", delivering the preferred perpetual/irrevocable paid-up outcome. Minor points short of the ideal preferred wording — the insolvency termination trigger in Section 12.4, and the fact that post-expiry irrevocability converts the grant to non-exclusive and attaches only to the Section 5.1.3 licences — are noted but are customary in this deal structure and are not material fallback failures.
